facts.raw_span: A man in his 50s with a 12-year history of recurrent follicular lymphoma
presented with a subacute, multifocal, pruritic, painful eruption
that began on the abdomen and then involved the scalp, groin, and extremities
He denied fevers, chills, weight loss, or other systemic symptoms
His medications included oxycodone, duvelisib (a PI3K inhibitor), and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
all started 14 months earlier for lymphoma management
well-demarcated erythematous plaques on the abdomen, axillae, and inguinal folds
scattered erythematous scaly papules and plaques on the scalp, extremities, and hands
confluent erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques with plate-like scales on the plantar feet
Two skin biopsies (abdomen and left foot) showed parakeratosis with collections of neutrophils
hypogranulosis, regular epidermal hyperplasia with elongated rete ridges, thin suprapapillary plates, dilated papillary dermal vessels, and dermal eosinophils
findings consistent with a psoriasiform drug reaction
